terms.gloss: bronze; a struck bronze instrument: a gong
terms.comment: Latin calls a bronze that is struck to make a sound simply aes, often in the plural: the hollow bronzes clashed in Bacchus’s procession in Ovid, the bell of the baths in Martial. No ancient source has the gong itself; the word for it is the classical one used of a modern thing, and ours. Where it must be told apart from a bell or cymbals, discus aēneus, a bronze disc, is a description of ours.

phrases.latin: inpulsaque tympana palmīs concavaque aera sonant longōque forāmine buxus
phrases.english: drums beaten with the palms, hollow bronzes, and the long-bored boxwood pipe resound
Give back the ball: the bell of the baths is ringing.
Can you hear the gongs? The dancers will come out soon.
Don’t bang the gong: the baby’s asleep.
